external_prior.source: Palmer Antarctica LTER 2011-12 Annual Report, seabird findings
external_prior.statement: Island-specific asymmetries were hypothesized to reflect loss of large penguin breeding groups, defined as groups in excess of 50 breeding pairs, citing Fraser and Patterson 1997.
external_prior.role: externally specified threshold fixed before this validation is opened

hypothesis: Islands retaining more >50-pair breeding groups at census year t should have higher / less-negative population growth from t to t+1 after accounting for island identity, current total abundance and secular year trend.
response: g_i,t+1 = log1p(N_i,t+1)-log1p(N_i,t); starting-zero intervals excluded, positive-to-zero transitions retained
primary_predictor: large_group_count_t = number of colony_code groups with breeding_pairs > 50 at year t; transform log1p and standardize in each training fold

models.G0: next_growth ~ island fixed effects + z(log1p current abundance) + z(year)

validation.scheme: leave-one-end-year-out with all islands of a held-out end-year excluded together
validation.support_rule: G1 MSE < G0 MSE AND full-data large-group coefficient > 0

fixed_sensitivity.predictor: fraction of current island breeding pairs occurring in >50-pair groups

interpretation_boundaries: This is an external-threshold validation using the same census, not an independent population dataset.
A positive result supports the historical large-group-loss hypothesis predictively but does not identify the causal benefit of large groups.
Do not search alternative pair thresholds after outcome access.
Do not treat colony-code groups as spatially equivalent without external mapping.
